instruction: Find electric cars for sale in the 33101 ZIP code within 25 miles, with a price cap of $35,000.

metadata.explanation: Variation 2: Changed to search in Miami area (ZIP 33101 instead of 10001), with lower price cap ($35,000 instead of $50,000), and smaller search radius (25 miles instead of 50). Keeps electric fuel type. Uses the same evaluator logic - parsing URL query parameters. No custom functions needed.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts URL query parameters from the active tab using get_active_tab_url_parse
Metric correctly compares extracted parameters with expected values using check_direct_json_object
All instruction requirements are covered: electric fuel type (fuel_slugs[]=electric), ZIP code (zip=33101), price limit (list_price_max=35000), and search radius (maximum_distance=25)
Expected values are semantically correct for cars.com URL query parameter format
String-based comparison is appropriate since URL query parameters are extracted as strings
Minor assumption about exact parameter names, but these are standard cars.com parameters observed in practice
Array parameter fuel_slugs[] extracted as single string value, which is acceptable for this single-value case
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider documenting that this evaluator assumes standard cars.com URL parameter format (list_price_max, maximum_distance, zip, fuel_slugs[])
For robustness against future website changes, could add alternative parameter name support if cars.com modifies their URL structure
If cars.com uses comma-separated values for fuel_slugs[] in some cases, consider adding split logic to handle multiple values (though not needed for this specific task)
